entries.clue: Satisfactory agreement includes indication of ‘more info soon’ (3,3)

indicatorNotes.includes: to include something is to take it in as a part, so NOD takes TBA inside itself

annotation.surface: Two parties reach a deal that is fine for now, with the details promised later.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'agreement' as a deal, but here it is a gesture of assent. NOT BAD is the grudging British way of saying something is fine.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial synonym: British understatement, where 'not bad' is mild praise meaning acceptable.

entries.clue: Errata corrected after end of election recount (7)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.corrected: something corrected is changed, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so the rearranged letters come behind the N

annotation.surface: Mistakes are fixed after a disputed election result is counted again.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes recount a second vote count; as the definition it is the verb meaning to tell a story.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the storytelling sense; the surface leans on the ballot-counting sense of recount instead.

entries.clue: Item of furniture ultimately not up to the task (5)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter counts

blocks.note: able = capable, up to the task

annotation.surface: A piece of furniture is too flimsy to do its job.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'ultimately not' as a single letter, not as a negative about the furniture.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one familiar kind of furniture, so the definition is broad on purpose.

entries.clue: A short product test covering America or somewhere in Europe (7)

indicatorNotes.short: something short is lacking length, so the word loses its tail letter
indicatorNotes.covering: to cover is to go over and around, so A TRIA wraps around US

annotation.surface: A quick trial of a product runs in the United States or in some European country.
annotation.walkthrough: America wants to be read as geography beside Europe, but it is only the two-letter abbreviation slotted inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by vague location: the clue only places the answer on the European map, leaving crossings to pin it down.

entries.clue: Gather everybody together at first for protest (6)

indicatorNotes.at first: 'at first' means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: to pick fruit is to gather it

annotation.surface: A rallying call to bring everyone together for a demonstration.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single call to protest; gather is really a verb for harvesting, and only the first letters of everybody together count.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a picket is a protest line of strikers outside a workplace, and to picket is to protest there.

entries.clue: One new, exclusive part of Oxford? (6)

annotation.surface: Someone asks about a new, elite college of Oxford University.
annotation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the city or the university but an Oxford, a laced leather shoe; the question mark flags that it is only one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example with a question mark: the inner lining is one component of an Oxford, a laced leather shoe.

entries.clue: Teacher, nurse, or typist, perhaps (3,6)

blocks.note: the essential staff kept working through the UK pandemic lockdowns
someone whose job is working at keys

annotation.surface: A list of ordinary jobs, as if from a careers form.
annotation.walkthrough: The typist looks like a third item on the same list, but a typist qualifies in a quite different sense: someone who works at keys.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the pandemic-era British label for essential staff, and a literal reading as someone working at keys.

entries.clue: Those people taking hit for rehab treatment (7)

indicatorNotes.taking: to take something is to take it in, so THEY holds RAP inside

blocks.note: a rap is a sharp hit

annotation.surface: People take a drug hit on their way into rehab.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes a hit a dose of a drug, which fits rehab; here it is a knock.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: recovering addicts are given treatment of this kind in rehab.

entries.clue: Good, alarming blow represented danger to us all? (6,7)

indicatorNotes.represented: to re-present is to present again in a new form, so the letters appear in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone hails a shocking setback as a good thing, then worries it threatens everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because the question mark admits it is a description rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description with a question mark: a planet-wide climate threat is a danger to everyone.

entries.clue: Dreary poet making comeback (4)

indicatorNotes.making comeback: a comeback is a return, so the word travels back the way it came

annotation.surface: A dull poet tries a comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare, so bard is a stock crossword poet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something dull and colourless.

entries.clue: Less deftly manipulated, like many online ‘experts’? (4-6)

indicatorNotes.manipulated: to manipulate is to handle and rework, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Clumsy handling is typical of internet pundits.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a jibe: online 'experts' often gave themselves the title.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: people who award themselves the title of expert online fit this adjective.

entries.clue: Rush job? (6)

annotation.surface: A hurried piece of work.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the phrase 'rush job'; split it and each word is a definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the verb for hurtling headlong, and the noun for a working life, which the question mark stretches to a job.

entries.clue: Running amok, Rambo captures a large, large castle (8)

indicatorNotes.Running amok: something running amok is out of control, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: The action hero goes on the rampage and seizes a very big castle.
annotation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the royal family's castle in Scotland. The repeated 'large' reads as emphasis but supplies two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is a named Scottish castle, the royal family's summer residence.

entries.clue: As a rule, information gathering consumes energy (9)

indicatorNotes.consumes: to consume is to take in, so the gathered pieces swallow E

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information

annotation.surface: Collecting data usually uses up power.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'information gathering' as one phrase; it is two separate pieces, with energy slotted between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both phrases mean usually, in most cases.

entries.clue: Source of comfort and serenity you initially found in each melody (4,5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its first letter
indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place is inside it, so SY lies within EACH

annotation.surface: Someone finds peace and comfort in every tune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found in each' looks like part of the serenity story, but it tells you the first letters go inside the word each.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a deep armchair gives the sitter comfort.

entries.clue: Fine old animal heading west (4)

indicatorNotes.heading west: in an across answer west is leftward, so the animal is written backwards

blocks.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox

annotation.surface: A fine elderly beast sets off westward.
annotation.walkthrough: Fine is the definition, not a compliment to the old animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean all right or acceptable.

entries.clue: Shame on you accepting a piece of work! (4)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take in, so the tut takes A inside itself

blocks.note: tsk is the tutting sound of disapproval

annotation.surface: Someone is scolded for taking on a job.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation is written as the clicking tut of disapproval, a word with no vowel until one is accepted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a job to be done.

entries.clue: They battle bulls and wild rooster (7)

indicatorNotes.wild: something wild is untamed and disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: Some fighters take on bulls and an untamed cockerel.
annotation.walkthrough: The farmyard picture suggests animals; the wild rooster is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: these Spanish bullfighters fight bulls on foot in the ring.

entries.clue: Put in the ground, or possibly let rot, say (3,2,4)

indicatorNotes.possibly: 'possibly' suggests another way the letters might be, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: Bury something, or else just leave it to decompose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a hedge on 'let rot' but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemistic idiom for burial, which the definition states plainly.

entries.clue: High-level betrayal requiring time, plus justification (7)

indicatorNotes.plus: plus means added on, so the second piece follows the first

annotation.surface: A traitor needs time and a good excuse.
annotation.walkthrough: High-level fits: this crime is betrayal of the state itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: betrayal of the state or sovereign, the gravest form of disloyalty.

entries.clue: Regular payment and bonus money put in post (7)

indicatorNotes.put in: to put one thing in another is to place it inside, so TIP goes within SEND

blocks.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is extra money for service

annotation.surface: Wages and a bonus are paid by mail.
annotation.walkthrough: Post is the verb for mailing, not a mailbox or a job.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fixed allowance or salary paid at intervals.

entries.clue: Empty container inside a different one (6)

indicatorNotes.inside: inside means within, so the first container sits within the second

blocks.note: a vat is another kind of container

annotation.surface: An empty box stands inside another box.
annotation.walkthrough: Empty is the definition, not a description of the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unoccupied, with nothing inside.

entries.clue: Make official statement supporting insurance case (8)

annotation.surface: Someone issues a formal statement backing an insurance claim.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface ties the statement to the case; supporting is only a short word for 'in favour of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: announcing something publicly and formally.

entries.clue: Bring out party drug (legal) (6)

annotation.surface: Someone produces a party drug, adding that it is legal.
annotation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'legal' looks like an aside but is a real piece, the opposite of illicit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: drawing out a response or fact.

entries.clue: Everything considered integral to criminal lawsuit (2,3)

indicatorNotes.integral to: something integral to a whole is built into it, so the answer lies within the words that follow

annotation.surface: Weighing everything up, some point is central to a court case.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, ending on the first letter of lawsuit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both phrases sum up the total.

entries.clue: Gross Texan regularly teases family members (5-5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

annotation.surface: A crude man from Texas mocks his relatives.
annotation.walkthrough: Gross reads as an insult for the Texan, but it is the unit of 144, abbreviated.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a parent's aunts belong to the wider family.

entries.clue: Provide help for a British sci-fi film (4)

annotation.surface: Someone asks for backing for a British science-fiction movie.
annotation.walkthrough: The film is American, so British is not describing it; it is just a one-letter abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to assist, usually in wrongdoing.

entries.clue: Branding activity in place for soft drink (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so PR goes inside SITE

annotation.surface: A marketing campaign is set up for a fizzy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt, as this is a heavily branded lemon-lime soda; branding activity is marketing, known by its two-letter abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is a lemon-lime soda brand.

entries.clue: Leaderless gang was in charge on a corner (6)

indicatorNotes.Leaderless: a leader goes in front, so leaderless means the first letter is dropped

annotation.surface: A gang without a boss, once in charge, hangs out on a street corner.
annotation.walkthrough: The gang lost its leader yet 'was in charge': the contradiction is the mechanism.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: something set at an angle sits as a corner would.
